title: No Bake Matcha Ganache Bars
description: These no bake matcha ganache bars are made with just 5 ingredients. The chewy matcha cookie dough base topped with creamy white chocolate matcha ganache is truly heavenly. Gluten free, dairy free, and refined sugar free.

hero.alt: A hand holding a no bake matcha ganache bar broken in half revealing the dark green chewy cookie dough base and bright green white chocolate matcha ganache layer with more bars in the background on a wooden board

thumbnail.alt: A hand holding a no bake matcha ganache bar broken in half showing the chewy green matcha base and creamy bright green ganache layer

instructions.text: Add the pitted dates, almond flour, and matcha to a food processor and blend until a dough forms.
Transfer the dough to a small lined container and press down very firmly, ensuring it is even.
In a saucepan, add the dairy-free white chocolate and coconut milk. Heat on low, stirring continuously, until the white chocolate is completely melted. Do not let it burn.
Remove from the heat and stir in the matcha powder until fully combined.
Let the ganache cool, then pour it on top of the pressed base.
Place in the freezer for 6 hours or overnight, until the ganache is set and holding its shape.
Sprinkle with extra matcha powder, slice, and enjoy!

notes: Press the base down very firmly — this helps it hold together when sliced.
Stir the ganache continuously on low heat so the white chocolate doesn't burn.
The ganache should be a spoonable consistency when set — creamy and able to hold its shape but not completely frozen.

story.subtitle: 5 ingredients
paragraphs: when you don't want to turn the oven on but still want something decadent, these no bake matcha white chocolate ganache bars are the move. these are up there as one of my favourite things i've made. i reach for no bake treats constantly in the warmer months, there's nothing better than pulling something cold and creamy straight from the fridge when it's too hot to think about baking.

the base is just three ingredients: pitted dates, almond flour and matcha, blitzed in a food processor until it forms a dough, then pressed firmly into a lined tin. the dates do all the sweetening and hold everything together with no added sugar or binder needed, while the almond flour keeps it gluten free and adds a slight nuttiness. press it down harder than feels necessary, that's what stops it falling apart once you slice it. once chilled, the texture sits somewhere between a chewy cookie and a dense energy ball.

the ganache is dairy-free white chocolate and thick canned coconut milk, melted together over low heat and stirred until smooth, with matcha whisked in right at the end off the heat. use the proper thick, full-fat canned kind here, not a thinner coconut milk from a carton, or it won't set. it goes into the freezer for 6 hours or overnight until it's holding its shape, more of a soft set custard than a firm chocolate ganache.

matcha quality matters more here than in a lot of other bakes, because the ganache flavour is quite delicate. organic ceremonial grade gives you the most vibrant colour and a rounder, less bitter flavour, culinary grade is more affordable and still works well. i prefer mine on the stronger side, so i lean towards the top of the range, but taste the ganache before adding more matcha and adjust from there.
love matcha? you'll also want my matcha marshmallows and easy healthy matcha cake.

what makes these worth it is the contrast, the chewy date base against the silky ganache. every bite is earthy, sweet and cold enough to actually feel refreshing. the first time i made these i didn't press the base down nearly hard enough, and it crumbled apart when i tried to lift a bar out, so now i really lean into it with the back of a spoon until it feels almost too firm.

if your no bake matcha ganache bars are very set, run a sharp knife under hot water and dry it before you cut, it goes through both layers without cracking the ganache, that way you get the cleanest slices. this is a small batch recipe that makes 6 thick bars but you can always opt for a bigger container or cut it into smaller slices to make more servings. since this recipe is super decadent and rich, small slices are very satisfying but i prefer big servings lol!

these keep in the fridge for up to 4 days or the freezer for up to a month. they're best eaten cold, since the ganache softens and loses its shape after 20 to 30 minutes at room temperature, so if you're taking these anywhere, keep them in the fridge until the last minute!

faq.question: How should I store matcha ganache bars?
faq.answer: Store in the fridge for up to 4 days, or in the freezer for up to 1 month. Let them thaw slightly before eating if frozen. I recommend running a sharp knife under hot water and drying it before slicing to get clean, even cuts without cracking the ganache layer.

faq.question: How set should the ganache be?
faq.answer: The ganache should be a spoonable consistency, not completely frozen but able to hold its shape. The texture is creamy without being runny. After 6 hours in the freezer it should be firm enough to slice cleanly. If the ganache still feels very soft after that time, pop it back in the freezer for another hour or two.

faq.question: Are these matcha ganache bars gluten free?
faq.answer: Yes. These bars are naturally gluten free as they are made with almond flour and contain no wheat or gluten flour. If you have a severe gluten sensitivity, check that your matcha powder, dates, and dairy-free white chocolate are certified gluten free, as some products can be processed in facilities that also handle gluten.

faq.question: Are these matcha ganache bars dairy free and refined sugar free?
faq.answer: Yes. The ganache is made with coconut milk and dairy free white chocolate, making the entire recipe dairy free. The base is naturally sweetened with dates and the white chocolate used is refined sugar free. Always check the label on your white chocolate to confirm it uses coconut sugar or another unrefined sweetener if you need the recipe to be fully refined sugar free.

faq.question: What type of matcha should I use?
faq.answer: I prefer using organic ceremonial grade matcha for the best nutrients, colour, and flavour. Ceremonial grade gives the most vibrant green colour and a sweeter, less bitter taste. Culinary grade matcha also works well and is more affordable, though the colour may be slightly less vivid. Avoid very cheap matcha powders as they can taste bitter and give a dull, greyish-green colour.

faq.question: Can I use regular white chocolate instead of dairy-free?
faq.answer: Yes, if you are not dairy free, you can absolutely use regular white chocolate in the ganache. The flavour and texture will be very similar. If you use regular white chocolate, the recipe will no longer be vegan or dairy free, but it will still be gluten free and refined sugar free if you choose a good quality white chocolate.

faq.question: My ganache isn't setting. What went wrong?
faq.answer: The most common reason the ganache doesn't set is too much liquid. Make sure you use thick canned coconut milk (the full-fat kind with a solid cream layer on top) and not a thinner coconut milk beverage or carton. The ratio of white chocolate to coconut milk matters too, so stick to the gram measurements. If the ganache still feels too liquid after mixing, allow it to cool at room temperature for 10 to 15 minutes before pouring over the base. This gives it a better chance of setting with the right texture.

faq.question: Can I make a larger batch of these matcha ganache bars?
faq.answer: Yes! Simply double all the ingredients and use a larger container. A standard 8x8 inch square tin works well for a double batch. Keep in mind that the ganache layer will be proportionally the same thickness, but you may need an extra hour in the freezer to ensure everything sets fully. Use a hot knife to slice neatly.

tips: I prefer a stronger matcha flavour so feel free to adjust the amount of matcha to your taste.
Press the base down very firmly so it holds together cleanly when sliced.
Use a larger container if you prefer thinner bars.
Run a sharp knife under hot water, dry it quickly, and use it to slice the bars — this gives you clean, smooth cuts through both the ganache and the base without cracking.

alternatives: Regular white chocolate (if not dairy free)
Oat milk white chocolate chips, melted
Cashew cream (thick, similar fat content, gives a slightly nuttier flavour)
Full-fat oat cream (works but the ganache may be slightly softer — allow extra freezing time)
Medjool dates give the best sticky, caramel-like texture — if using smaller Deglet Noor dates, you may need a few extra
A combination of almond flour and 3 tablespoons maple syrup can substitute if dates are unavailable, though the base will be slightly less chewy
